# Exact three-probability face support and its payment frontier

This note computes the entire three-coordinate zero-diagonal support, including its boundary regimes. It then states precisely the remaining probability inequality for the actual three-full-row tetrahedral configuration. No assertion that arbitrary probabilities, or arbitrary common-centroid cuts, satisfy that remaining inequality is made.

## 1. Support and exact maximizers

Let h_2(W) be the maximum of

    sum_i W_i sqrt(Z_ij Z_ik),

over nonnegative, zero-diagonal, column-stochastic three by three matrices Z; in each summand {i,j,k}={1,2,3}. Let P_i>0 and W_i=sqrt(P_i). Define

    e2=P_1P_2+P_1P_3+P_2P_3,  e3=P_1P_2P_3.

If all three reciprocal triangle inequalities hold,

    1/P_i <= 1/P_j+1/P_k,                            (1)

then the exact, attained support is

    h_2(sqrt(P))=e2/(2 sqrt(e3)).                    (2)

Otherwise there is a unique index i for which (1) fails, and

    h_2(sqrt(P))=sqrt(P_j+P_k).                      (3)

The formulas agree on a reciprocal-triangle boundary. In particular the inequalities in (1) are non-strict and no limiting maximizer is needed.

Proof. For arbitrary eta_i>=0 satisfying

    4 eta_j eta_k >= W_i^2,

weighted AM-GM bounds every row contribution by eta_j Z_ij+eta_k Z_ik. Summing columns gives the upper bound sum eta_i.

In (1), set eta_i=W_jW_k/(2W_i)=sqrt(e3)/(2P_i) and H=sum eta_i. Condition (1) is exactly 2eta_i<=H. The actual matrix

    Z_ij=(H/2-eta_i)/eta_j  (i!=j),  Z_ii=0

is nonnegative and has column sums one. Its row-i objective contribution is H-2eta_i, so the total is H=e2/(2sqrt(e3)). This attains the AM-GM upper bound.

If (1) fails at i, put S=P_j+P_k. Its failure is precisely P_i<P_jP_k/S. Choose

    eta_i=sqrt(S)/2,
    eta_j=P_k/(2sqrt(S)), eta_k=P_j/(2sqrt(S)).

The constraints for rows j,k are equalities, and the remaining constraint holds because 4eta_jeta_k=P_jP_k/S>P_i. Their sum is sqrt(S). Attainment is explicit: row i is zero; column j goes entirely to row k and column k entirely to row j; column i has entries P_j/S in row j and P_k/S in row k. Its objective is sqrt(S). This proves (3). At equality P_i=P_jP_k/S the same construction and value are valid, as is the preceding construction. At most one strict reciprocal triangle inequality can fail, since each such failure says one positive reciprocal exceeds the sum of the other two. This proves all claims.

If a probability is zero, continuity or direct optimization gives sqrt(P_j+P_k); if two vanish the value is sqrt(P_i). The compact matrix domain justifies continuity and attainment also at these degeneracies.

## 2. Exact tetrahedral face payment

For zero-diagonal geometric-mean support h_3 in four coordinates, the proved coordinate-face identity gives

    h_3(P_1^(1/3),P_2^(1/3),P_3^(1/3),0)
      =h_2(sqrt(P_1),sqrt(P_2),sqrt(P_3))^(2/3).     (4)

The identity follows by maximizing the fourth-column allocation with Holder; its complete proof and equality allocation are in `candidate df39f37487bbac05`.

Consequently (4) is at least one whenever a pair sum P_j+P_k is at least one. This conclusion does not require locating the support regime: the explicit two-row matrix from Section 1 already supplies the value sqrt(P_j+P_k). If all pair sums are less than one, a reciprocal-triangle failure necessarily gives support less than one. If all reciprocal triangle inequalities hold, payment is exactly

    e2^2 >= 4e3.                                    (5)

All quantities before squaring are positive. Strict inequalities give a strictly improving zero-diagonal competitor. Equality gives an attained paying competitor, which is sufficient for a global support bound but by itself need not strictly improve a global maximizer.

## 3. Exact frontier in the cross-split orientation

For the actual unresolved tetrahedral configuration, orient all sections toward the unique noncentral vertex. Write a,b,c for the corresponding cap probabilities, with the b-section projectively between the other two. The actually oriented full rows have probabilities

    (P_X,P_Y,P_Z)=(a,1-b,c).                        (6)

Thus a>=b or c>=b already pays by a pair sum. Also a+c>=1 already pays. Only

    0<a,c<b<1,  a+c<1                              (7)

can remain. Put s=a+c, t=1-b. In the reciprocal-triangle regime, condition (5) becomes

    [ac+s t]^2 >= 4ac t.                           (8)

Its two roots as a quadratic in t are

    t_minus=ac/(1+sqrt(1-s))^2,
    t_plus =ac/(1-sqrt(1-s))^2.                    (9)

Indeed the discriminant is 16a^2c^2(1-s). The reciprocal inequality for the probability t requires t>=ac/s. Since (1+sqrt(1-s))^2>s, this implies t>t_minus. Therefore, within this regime, the EXACT payment frontier is

    1-b >= ac/(1-sqrt(1-a-c))^2.                  (10)

This formulation keeps both outer cap values separately and neither assumes they agree nor replaces actual tetrahedral volume by an arbitrary probability law. In particular the raw cubic (8) cannot be applied outside the reciprocal-triangle regime: its small-t branch can be positive even though the true support is sqrt(a+c)<1.

The interior formula in Section 1 recovers the formula already used in the one-full/two-zero stratum. The additional content here is the exhaustive boundary description, explicit boundary maximizers, and exact remaining frontier (10). The actual common-centroid geometry needed to establish payment in the remaining branch has not been proved in this note.
